payload.text: Paper finding INV-M (docs/truth-ledger-paper-v2.md, Appendix A): a claim's --paths can be filed as a glob that matches zero tracked files -- most concretely, space-separated paths ('a.sh b.sh') silently store as one literal path matching nothing. The claim's hash still matches, a verifier still agrees, and the invalidation trigger can never fire -- the protection is decorative. Not hypothetical here: tr-3591aae0 hit exactly this (evidence_paths stored as a single space-joined string), found by inspection, retracted, superseded by tr-94a98135 with correct comma-separated paths. Currently mitigated only by the operating convention (file a successor, retract the original), not a gate. Fix (already scoped in the paper): an intake check refusing (a) whitespace-containing path entries with no comma, and (b) any path/glob that matches zero tracked files at filing time; plus a canary fault seeding a dead tripwire and asserting the new check refuses it. Lands in the truth-ledger template (scripts/truth, truth-canary.sh, ADR + paper Appendix A row for INV-M's promotion from proposed to shipped), then syncs back here via copier update, same shape as the ADR-006/F7 cycle.
